Types of Traffic Signs in UAE

UAE Traffic signs are categorized into several groups. They are based on their functions. These include Mandatory, Warning, Prohibitory, Control, and Guide signs. Let’s break down each category for better understanding:

1. Mandatory Traffic Signs

Mandatory signs provide clear instructions that drivers must follow. They indicate required actions, such as which direction to drive or speed limits to adhere to. These signs are typically circular and feature clear symbols and instructions. Common examples of mandatory signs include:

  • Turn Right Only: Indicates that the driver must turn right.
  • Ahead Only: Drivers must continue straight; no other direction allowed.
  • 60 km/h Freeway: A speed limit sign. It indicates the maximum speed on the road, which is 60 km/h.
  • Keep Right / Keep Left: Directs drivers to keep to the right or left side of the road. However, it depends on the sign.
  • Pass Either Side: Allows vehicles to overtake on either lane’s side.

2. Warning Traffic Signs

Warning signs alert drivers to potential hazards ahead. So that they can take precautions to avoid accidents. These signs come triangular shape with a red border. A symbol depicting the risk. Common warning signs in the UAE include:

  • Curves Ahead (Left/Right): Alerts drivers about sharp turns ahead.
  • Pedestrian Crossing: It indicates areas where pedestrians cross the road.
  • T-Junction: Warns drivers, a T-junction is ahead.
  • Maximum Headroom: Informs drivers of height restrictions. Important for larger vehicles or trucks.
  • Slippery Road: Signals that road conditions may be slippery, particularly in wet weather.

3. Prohibitory Road Signs

Prohibitory signs communicate actions that are not allowed. These signs are generally circular with a red border and a symbol indicating the prohibited action. Some of the most common prohibitory signs in the UAE include:

  • No Left/Right Turn: At a certain intersection, turning left or right isn’t allowed.
  • No Overtaking: Prohibits overtaking in a specific road section.
  • Speed Limit Exceeded: Warns against exceeding the speed limits.
  • No U-Turn: At a particular location, this indicates that U-turns are not allowed.
  • No Parking: Signals that parking is not allowed in that area.

Parking in a restricted zone = AED 500 fine

4. Control Signs

Control signs provide instructions regarding traffic flow, right of way, and access restrictions. They help in managing the movement of vehicles and pedestrians. Key control signs in the UAE include:

  • Stop: A red, octagonal sign means drivers must come to a complete stop.
  • Give Way: Drivers give way to traffic from another direction.
  • Yield to Pedestrians: Drivers must stop and yield to pedestrians at crossings.
  • One-Way: Traffic must flow in a single direction.

5. Parking Control Signs

Parking control signs indicate where parking is allowed/prohibited. Also, these road traffic signs in UAE may specify time limits for parking for certain groups. Examples include:

  • 🚫 No Parking: Indicates areas where parking is prohibited.
  • ⏱️ Timed Parking: Shows the maximum parking duration in a particular area.
  • ♿ Reserved Parking for People of Determination: Reserved parking spaces for people with special needs. However, a permit is required.

6. Guide and Exit Direction Signs

Guide signs help drivers navigate roads by providing directional information. These signs may include names of streets, exit signs, or directions to key locations. Common examples include:

  • 📍 City Center Sign: Points toward the direction of the city center.
  • 🛣️ Emirates Route Sign: Shows the direction to different emirates in the UAE.
  • ✈️ Airport Sign: Directs drivers to the nearest airport.
  • Exit Lane Sign: Provides information about the correct lane to use before exiting a highway or motorway.

7. Hazard Marker Signs

Hazard marker signs indicate potential risks or obstacles along the roadside. These traffic signs in UAE are typically used to warn drivers of physical hazards like guardrails, bridges, or islands. Common hazard marker signs in the UAE include:

  • Single Chevron Right/Left: Indicates that a sharp curve is approaching on the road.
  • Multiple Chevron Right/Left: Warns of a more pronounced bend ahead.
  • T-Junction Chevron: A specific marker for an upcoming T-junction.

8. Temporary & Digital Signs

Often missed but very important.

  •  Roadworks Ahead 🚧
  •  Diversion Routes
  •  Electronic Display Boards (show accidents, speed updates, lane closures)

Special Signs for People of Determination

The United Arab Emirates is committed to its citizens and visitors alike. They want assurance of accessibility for all drivers. For this, special parking spots are provided for people with disabilities. Specifically, those with disabilities are marked with a blue “P” symbol. Alongside a figure in a wheelchair. Note that you must obtain a permit to park in these designated areas. You cannot park in these spots without this permit. Parking here without a permit = AED 1,000 fine + 4 black points.

FAQs on UAE Traffic Signs

Q1. What common traffic signs in UAE should I know when driving?

The common signs you will witness while passing down the roads are speed limits, stop signs, no entry, and roundabout warnings. Follow them strictly to avoid any fines.

Q2. What does “Salik” signage mean in Dubai?

It refers to Dubai’s electronic toll gate system. It deducts toll fees automatically from your prepaid account when passing under the gates.

Q3. Are traffic signs in English and Arabic?

Yes, all signs display both languages, helping both tourists and locals to understand.

Q4. How are speed limits displayed on highways?

The speed limit is displayed on the side of the highway on white circular signs with red borders. It shows speed limits in kilometres per hour.

Q5. What signs indicate toll roads or special zones?

Blue Salik signs mark toll roads; brown signs often show tourist zones.

Q6. What should I do if I miss or misunderstand a sign?

Don’t take any sudden moves. Stay calm and follow road rules. Correct your route safely.

Q7. What’s the fine for parking in a disabled spot without a permit?

AED 1,000 + 4 black points.
